name: Joules per token across the corpus spans 4.11 to 20.53 on comparable batch-1 rows, but three rows had to be excluded - an unsourced figure, three multi-GPU runs charging one card's TDP, and a batch-2048 row whose real batch is 16x larger than batch 1
symptom: The corpus has both TDP for 116 accelerators and decode_tok_s for 32 benchmark records, so joules per token looks like a straightforward join. The naive join produces absurd figures: the GB200 NVL72 row at 0.16 J/tok, which would make a 27kW rack-scale system the most energy-efficient device in the database by a factor of 25, and the Cerebras WSE-3 at 36.00 J/tok against its own 27,000W TDP on a 750 tok/s vendor peak figure.
root_cause:
Three separate confounds, each of which invalidates the join for specific rows.

UNITS OF DEVICE. sglang-deepseek-v3-gb200-nvl72-decode-tps-per-node aggregates an entire NVL72 rack, but the TDP joined to it is a single 1200W accelerator figure. Dividing rack throughput by one card's power understates the true consumption by two orders of magnitude. The same defect hits comm-mi50-50x rows, which scale via HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES across 2, 4, 8 and 16 GPUs while the accelerator record carries one MI50X's 300W.

MEASUREMENT BOUNDARY. The Cerebras figure is a vendor peak number on a 750 tok/s claim with no stated power at the measured operating point; 27,000W is a board TDP, not the draw during that benchmark. The apple m4-pro joules records are system- and package-level figures that must never be mixed with a GPU TDP - a different boundary entirely.

BATCH SIZE. comm-mi50-8x and comm-mi50-16x run at -b 2048 -ub 1024, i.e. micro-batch 2048. A batch-2048 throughput divided by a card's TDP is not comparable to a batch-1 row, because per-token energy falls as batch rises: the batch is doing the work of sharing fixed cost, and it also means the figure is not what a single user experiences.

UNSOURCED VALUE. local-rtx-5070-13b-q4-decode is marked UNSOURCED, DO NOT CITE and was decommissioned on 2026-10-04, retained only for history because the schema forbids nulling value. It produces an attractive 2.08 J/tok that is the second-best in the naive table and must not be quoted.
workaround:
Restrict to rows that are single-device, batch 1, and carrying a sourced value. Nine rows qualify:

  J/tok   $/Mtok   accelerator                    W     tok/s  batch  model
   4.11   0.1017   nvidia-rtx-5090                 575   140.00  b1     Qwen3-14B-AWQ
   4.87   0.1204   amd-radeon-ai-pro-r9700         300    61.66  b1     Bonsai-27B Q1_0
   5.54   0.1371   nvidia-rtx-5080                 360    65.00  b1     Qwen3 32B
   6.76   0.1674   nvidia-rtx-5090                 575    85.00  b1     Qwen3 32B
   7.54   0.1867   amd-radeon-rx-7900-xtx          355    47.06  b1     Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL
  10.91   0.2700   nvidia-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell   600    55.00  b1     Llama 3.3 70B
  12.78   0.3163   nvidia-rtx-5090                 575    45.00  b1     Llama 3.3 70B
  13.71   0.3394   local-apple-m5-ultra           480    35.00  b1     Llama 3.3 70B
  20.53   0.5081   amd-instinct-mi300x             750    36.53  b1     DeepSeek-V3 671B Q4_K_M

Electricity cost at the corpus's own $0.0891/kWh rate from supply/us-electricity-industrial-tariff-2024, using 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ.

WHAT IT MEANS: energy efficiency and cost of ownership disagree, and the corpus proves it. The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell at 10.91 J/tok is 2.65x less energy-efficient than the RTX 5080 at 5.54, yet the 5080 is $6,550 against the PRO 6000's $16,624 and cannot fit a 70B model at all. The 5090's own rows span 4.11 to 12.78 J/tok depending purely on which model runs - a 3.1x range on identical hardware, which is larger than the spread between any two different cards here.

Energy is therefore a poor proxy for value on this corpus, and the joules-per-token framing should be read as a statement about heat and power draw, not about what to buy. value-tco-and-why-rent-vs-own-cannot-be-computed-from-this-corpus reaches the same conclusion from the cost side: power is 15-20% of three-year cost for $2,000 cards and under 5% above $12,000.
notes:
FILED 2026-10-11 (parent, in place of a subagent that died on HTTP 429 after 6 API calls, before writing anything). Computed directly from the accelerator TDP fields and decode_tok_s benchmark records.

Rows excluded and why: local-rtx-5070-13b-q4-decode (UNSOURCED, decommissioned); comm-mi50-8x-gpt-oss-120b-mxfp4-decode-collapse and comm-mi50-16x-deepseek-v32-awq-reported (multi-GPU against one card's TDP, and batch 2048); the GB200 NVL72 decode record, benchmarks/sglang-deepseek-v3-gb200-nvl72-decode-tps-per-node (rack-scale against one card's TDP; omitted from affects because it has no source record, which is itself a gap worth noting); alt-cerebras-gpt56-ultrafast-tps (vendor peak with no measured power at that operating point).

The GB200 exclusion deserves a note: a per-node figure divided by a single accelerator's TDP is not merely imprecise, it is wrong by the number of cards in the node. Any future joules-per-token row in this corpus must state the device count the power figure covers, and the batch size, alongside the J/tok.
